field: content_html (PEGI/BBFC section) + conclusion_html + key_fact box + glossary_terms + flashcard_questions
wrong_text: The BBFC (British Board of Film Classification) classifies films for cinema and home release with ratings including U (suitable for all), PG (parental guidance), 12A, 15 and 18.
problem: The BBFC certificate list is incomplete. It omits the '12' certificate, which exists alongside 12A. 12A is cinema-only (under-12s admitted with an adult); '12' is the home video/physical media equivalent (no under-12s may purchase or rent, no adult exemption). OCR R093 mark schemes expect students to know both. The current full teaching set is U, PG, 12A/12, 15, 18. The lesson refers only to 12A throughout, which would cause a student to miss the 12 certificate in an exam.
correction: Change the BBFC rating list to: 'U (suitable for all), PG (parental guidance), 12A (cinema: under-12s admitted with an adult), 12 (home video: no one under 12 may purchase or rent), 15 and 18.' Update the key-fact box, conclusion bullet, PEGI/BBFC common-mistake collapsible, glossary PEGI definition, and flashcard answer for 'What does the BBFC classify?' to note both 12A (cinema) and 12 (home video) exist. Also update the practice question mark scheme for the 4-mark 'describe the difference' question to include 12 as an acceptable BBFC example.
